details: The United Nations has revised down its 2026 global economic growth forecast to 2.5%, a decrease from its January projection of 2.7%. This reduction, coupled with an anticipated rise in global inflation to 3.9%, is primarily attributed to escalating crises in the Middle East and the resulting surge in oil prices. The report highlights that developing economies are expected to face higher inflation rates, and Western Asia is projected to experience the most severe economic damage.
title: UN Cuts Global Growth Outlook to 2.5% Over Mideast Energy Crisis

details: Escalating military tensions between the US and Iran, including Iran's continued threat to the Strait of Hormuz—a crucial oil shipping lane—are keeping global oil prices elevated above $100 per barrel. While US President Donald Trump has suggested the conflict could end "very quickly," he also warned of potential renewed strikes if nuclear talks fail. This ongoing instability contributes to global inflation and monetary policy uncertainty.
title: US-Iran Tensions Sustain High Oil Prices, Strait of Hormuz Risks

details: The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, a significant piece of legislation aimed at establishing a comprehensive regulatory framework for digital assets, was advanced by the US Senate Banking Committee on May 14, 2026. The bill seeks to classify various digital assets (digital commodities, investment contract assets, and permitted payment stablecoins) and address critical issues like stablecoin yield. This move is seen as a step towards providing regulatory certainty, potentially attracting more institutional capital into the crypto market, despite ongoing debates regarding certain provisions.
title: US Senate Committee Passes CLARITY Act for Digital Asset Framework

details: The Central Bank of Ireland (CBI) has issued a Notice of Intention to integrate new knowledge and competence requirements for crypto-asset services into its Minimum Competency Code, effective July 28, 2026. This initiative aligns with the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) and aims to ensure that staff providing advice or information on crypto-assets possess the necessary expertise, thereby enhancing investor protection in the rapidly evolving digital asset space.
title: Irish Central Bank Sets New Crypto-Asset Competency Rules
